[Statistical software from my research, and three apps built on the side.]{.lead-line}

## Research software

### klue

[R package · [GitHub](https://github.com/o-frings/klue) · [R-universe](https://o-frings.r-universe.dev/klue)]{.meta}

An R package implementing the specification rule for latent class logit models from the [companion paper](research.qmd#classes-or-continuum). It estimates latent class models from clustering-based starting values, fits the mixed logit benchmark, and reports BIC, AIC, ICL, and entropy diagnostics.

```r
install.packages("klue", repos = "https://o-frings.r-universe.dev")
```

### Net climate value pipeline

[R pipeline · To be made accessible upon publication]{.meta}

The reproducible R pipeline behind *The Net Climate Value of Carbon Credits* ([paper](research.qmd#net-climate-value)): data, calibration, and simulation code.

## Side projects

Yalla and Clue are free and work offline, with your data stored on the device. Signing in is optional and syncs your data across devices. Both are plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript without a build step and install on the iPhone home screen as progressive web apps.

### Yalla

[Offline-first workout tracker · [App](https://o-frings.github.io/yalla/) · [GitHub](https://github.com/o-frings/yalla)]{.meta}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="More"}
It tracks training volume across twelve muscle groups, shown as a balance radar, and suggests deload weeks from cumulative load. It builds plans around your venue (home, park, gym) and logged injuries. Volume for bodyweight exercises counts body weight plus any added weight. When signed in, you can share workouts with friends and opt in to a push reminder when you have not trained for two days. On iPhone and iPad, a Shortcut adds finished workouts to Apple Health.
:::

### Clue

[Knowledge and debate trainer · [App](https://o-frings.github.io/clue/) · [GitHub](https://github.com/o-frings/clue)]{.meta}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="More"}
New cards turn up in a discovery feed and open in layers, starting with the gist. A simplified SM-2 spaced-repetition schedule brings cards back for review. A map of what you know grows as you learn and shows cards due for review as faded nodes. Every card cites sources from an evidence registry, which records the strength of evidence for each source.
:::

### Mäander

[Bike routing for quiet, nature-oriented rides in Germany]{.meta}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="More"}
Mäander (TypeScript, MapLibre, BRouter) uses a custom routing profile that favours parks and forests and avoids busy roads. Motorways carry a 700 m noise halo, and forest tracks cost a fraction of paved roads. One slider moves a route from fastest to greenest. It also plans round trips of a chosen length and compass direction and compares several route alternatives side by side.
:::
